text:
sanjay: seeing a weird oscillation on prod for several int4 models on SM89. p50 spikes for mid-seq (512-1024) after ~3 hours of steady traffic. looks like kernel picks are flipping between int4_v2 and fp8_v1 and kv-cache gets thrash-y. logs attached below.

kevin: can you paste the profiler snippet? wondering if batch size changes are triggering a different kernel path.

sanjay: here are the relevant lines from the pick log + perf counters:
```
# pick-log
seq=768 model=llama2-70b quant=int4_v2 -> fp8_v1 (chosen)
kernel_latency_ms: int4_v2=14.2 fp8_v1=10.8 (cold)
runtime_switch_cost_ms=18.4
kv_cache_miss_rate spike: 0.03 -> 0.27
batch_size distribution: 1,1,2,1,4,1,1,1 (p50 1 -> p90 3)
```
profiling: small blowup on `kv_write_lock` and an extra memcpy on fp8 path after switch.

olivia: hmm that runtime_switch_cost looks huge vs the delta. if switching cost > latency delta caching will lose. do we have the autotuner hysteresis configured?

maria: currently seqlen_penalty is 0.12 and hysteresis_window_ms is 10 for SM89 in the quant_profiles. that's probably too small for midseq churn.

kevin: theory: when batches briefly grow to 3-4 tokens, pickbench favors int4_v2 (good for throughput) but when seq distribution changes the kernel pick flips to fp8_v1 (better memory footprint at this seqlen) — the flip invalidates/performs a KV-format handling path causing memcpy and kv_lock contention. net result p50 increases.

olivia: quick experiment ideas: 1) increase hysteresis_window_ms to 40 for SM89-int4 profiles, 2) add a minimum hold_time_ms after switching before allowing revert, 3) disable auto-switch for seqlen in [512,1024] for impacted models and force fp8 path as a short-term fallback.

sanjay: ran a canary against clone-prod traffic on dedicated pool with option (1) + tiny hold_time_ms=25. results: p50 reduced from 155ms -> 118ms and kv_miss spike gone. p90 unchanged.

maria: can you paste the canary command?

sanjay: `./run-canary --pool sm89-prod-canary --model llama2-70b --seq 768 --patch "quant_profiles.sm89.seqlen_hysteresis_ms=40; quant_profiles.sm89.min_hold_ms=25"`

kevin: nice. what's the CPU/GPU utilization delta?

sanjay: GPU util ~72% -> 74% (small), CPU kernel_thread wait events dropped ~2.8x. overall cost slightly up (~+3%) but latency stability is better.

olivia: +1 to ship a hotfix: bump hysteresis and add a targeted rule: for models tagged `high-midseq` on SM89, prefer fp8 if seqlen in [512,1024] until we have a longer-term KV-format-path fix.

maria: I'll author a tiny runtime patch: `seqlen_force_mode = {sm89: {range: [512,1024], mode: "prefer_fp8", ttl_hr: 6}}` and a toggle in configstore. will open PR.

kevin: please also add a metric for `kernel_switch_count` per-minute and alert if > 5 for a model over 5m. that will catch regressions earlier.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary-id=canary-20231107-004, targets=sm89-prod-canary, config-patch-id=cfg-7892, initiated-by=maria

sanjay: thanks — will follow up after 30m and paste perf histograms. if stable we roll to remaining SM89 pools with gradual ramp. :thumbsup:

olivia: followup: we should also add an autotuner unit test that simulates bouncing batch sizes + midseq distribution so picks don't oscillate. low-priority ticket created: INFRA-4321.

maria: PR open: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/1234 — includes the config toggle + docs + a small unit-test for seqlen hysteresis.

kevin: great work. if this reappears after hotfix we'll need to dig into the fp8 memcpy path and possible kv-format versioning bug.

sanjay: agree. I'll keep monitoring.
